6d7eea7239.d: The eclipse is already in progress at moonrise (grastodaya). Umbral magnitude: 0.37 (parimāṇa ≈4.5 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:26►19:53 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

6d8dee03d7.s:
smr̥tyantarē---  
amā pātaśca saṅkrāntistathā vaidhr̥tirēva ca।  
aṣṭakāścaiva manvādiryugādiśca mahālayaḥ॥  
candrasūryōparāgaśca gajacchāyā tathaiva ca।  
dravyabrāhmaṇasampattiḥ śrāddhakālāḥ prakīrtitāḥ॥  
manvantarādayō matsyapurāṇē darśitāḥ---  
āśvayukchuklanavamī kārtikī dvādaśī sitā।  
tr̥tīyā caitramāsasya sitā bhādrapadasya ca॥  
phālgunasyāpyamāvāsyā puṣyasyaikādaśī sitā।  
āṣāḍhasyāpi daśamī māghamāsasya saptamī॥  
śrāvaṇasyāṣṭamī kr̥ṣṇā tathā''ṣāḍhī ca pūrṇimā।  
kārtikī phālgunī caitrī jyaiṣṭhī pañcadaśī sitā॥  
manvantarādayaścaitē dattasyākṣayakārakāḥ।  
kr̥taṁ śrāddhaṁ vidhānēna manvādiṣu yugādiṣu॥  
hāyanāni dvisāhasraṁ pitr̥̄ṇāṁ tr̥ptidaṁ bhavēt।  
āsu snānaṁ japō hōmaḥ puṇyānantyāya kalpatē॥  
mahābhāratē'pi---   
yā manvādyā yugādyāśca tithayastāsu mānavaḥ।  
snātvā bhuktvā ca dattvā ca tadanantaphalaṁ labhēt॥  
kālādarśē'pi---  
manvādyāsu yugādyāsu pradattaḥ salilāñjaliḥ।  
sahasravārṣikī tr̥ptiṁ pitr̥̄ṇāmāvahēt parām॥  
dvisahasrābdikī tr̥ptiṁ kr̥taṁ śrāddhaṁ yathāvidhi।  
snānaṁ dānaṁ japō hōmaḥ puṇyānantyāya kalpatē॥  
puruṣārthacintāmaṇau manuḥ---  
sahasraguṇitaṁ dānaṁ bhavēddattaṁ yugādiṣu।  
karma śrāddhādikaṁ caiva tathā manvantarādiṣu॥

6dc8785d39.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and budhaḥ in puṣyaḥ karkaṭaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°33′11.30″.
6dc8785d39.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°33′11.30″, 0°32′53.14″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at puṣyaḥ-4 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 0°29′57.09″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.79, elongation 12°31′24.39″ W). budhaḥ at puṣyaḥ-4 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 1°03′08.38″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.26, elongation 12°33′25.75″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

6e0df71486.d: One must not bathe in many (small) rivers during the rainy season. Especially for the first three days of Karkataka masa, these rivers are impure. However, this does not apply to the Mahanadis, owing to their greatness, including Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Godavari, Kaveri, Shona, Penna, and the Pancha Gangas (Kaveri, Tungabhadra, Krishnaveni, Gautami, Bhagirathi). Exceptions are made in the case of Upakarma, Utsarga, Grahanam, Preta snanam etc., and when new water can be mixed in these rivers, and when there is a lack of other water sources.
6e0df71486.s:
atriḥ---  
siṁhakarkaṭayōrmadhyē sarvā nadyō rajasvalāḥ।  
na snānādīni karmāṇi tāsu kurvīta mānavaḥ॥  
yōgayājñavalkyaḥ---  
rajōduṣṭē'mbhasi snānaṁ varjyaṁ nadyādiṣu dvijaiḥ।  
kadarthitaṁ rajastēṣāṁ sandhyōpāstiśca tarpaṇam  
vyāghrapādaḥ---  
siṁhakarkaṭayōrmadhyē sarvā nadyō rajasvalāḥ।  
tāsu snānaṁ na kurvīta varjayitvā samudragāḥ॥  
kātyāyanaḥ---  
karkaṭādau rajōduṣṭā gōmatī vāsaratrayam।  
candrabhāgā satī sindhuḥ sarayūnarmadā tathā॥  
atrāpavādamāha marīciḥ---  
ādityaduhitā gaṅgā plakṣajātā sarasvatī।  
rajasā nābhibhūyantē yē cānyē nadasaṁjñitāḥ॥  
mārkaṇḍēyaḥ---  
kālindī gautamī gaṅgā vēṇikā ca sarasvatī।  
sāmarthyādābhijātyāca rajō nābhibhavatyamūḥ॥  
jāhnavyādityasambhūtā plakṣajātā sarasvatī।  
rajasā naiva duṣyanti nadāḥ kr̥ṣṇā ca vēṇikā॥  
vāmanapurāṇē---  
sarasvatī nadī puṇyā tathā vaitaraṇī nadī।  
āpagā ca mahāpuṇyā gaṅgā mandākinī tathā॥  
madhupravāhāṁ'śumatī kauśikī pāpanāśinī।  
dr̥ṣadvatī mahāpuṇyā tathā vaitaraṇī nadī॥  
ētāsāmudakaṁ puṇyaṁ varṣākālē pravarddhitam।  
rajasvalātvamētāsāṁ vidyatē na kadācana॥  
yamaḥ---  
gaṅgā dharmōdbhavā puṇyā yamunā ca sarasvatī।  
antargatarajōyōgāḥ sarvāhaḥsvapi cāmalāḥ॥  
kālādarśaḥ---  
siṁhakarkaṭayōrnadyaḥ sarvā ēva rajasvalāḥ।  
tridinaṁ syurmahānadyō gōdāṁ pēṇṇāṁ sarasvatīm।  
bhāgīrathīṁ ca kālindī nadān śōṇādikān vinā॥  
kēcittu–--  
yā nissr̥tā nadāḥ prōktā yāśca gaṅgēti kīrtitāḥ।  
ētāsāṁ karkaṭē bhānau rajōdōṣō na vidyatē॥  
kāvērītuṅgabhadrā ca kr̥ṣṇavēṇī ca gautamī।  
bhāgīrathī ca vikhyātā pañcagaṅgāḥ prakīrtitāḥ॥  
kātyāyanaḥ---  
upākarmaṇi cōtsargē prētasnānē tathaiva ca।  
candrasūryagrahē caiva rajōdōṣō na vidyatē॥  
mahadambusamaṁ vā'pi yadi tiṣṭhēt purātanam।  
navāmbu miśritaṁ tēna na duṣṭamiti sūrayaḥ॥   
vyāghrapādaḥ---  
abhāvē kūpavāpīnāmanapāyipayōbhr̥tām।  
rajōduṣṭē'pi payasi grāmabhōgō na duṣyati॥

6eab61fefa.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°54′42.77″, 0°54′30.00″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°07′32.67″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.97, elongation 14°48′02.59″ E). śukraḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°12′49.91″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.90, elongation 14°41′59.03″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
6eab61fefa.s:
bhāvābhāvāya lōkānāṁ kalpanēyaṁ pradarśitā।  
svamārgagāḥ prayāntyētē dūramanyōnyamāśritāḥ॥  
--sūryasiddhāntē  
  
ṣaṇmāsaṁ grahabhinnabhaṁ tyaja śubhē yauddhaṁ tathōtpātabham।  
--muhūrtacintāmaṇau (nāradasaṁhitānusārēṇa)

6eddf856c4.b: Observed on Śukla-Prathamā tithi of Śrāvaṇaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
6eddf856c4.d: Śrāvaṇa-māsaḥ begins today --- In the Mahābhārata, it is said that one who observes the entire month of Śrāvaṇa with self-restraint and partakes only in a single meal per day (ekabhakta), obtains the fruits of taking bath in various holy waters and his family lineage prospers (jñātivardhanaḥ). In the Vāmana Purāṇa, it is said that, to please Śrīdhara (a form of Viṣṇu) during the month of Śrāvaṇa, the wise should offer ghee, pots of milk, cows that give ghee, and fruits, all with devotion.
6eddf856c4.s:
śrāvaṇakr̥tyaṁ mahābhāratē---  
śrāvaṇaṁ niyatō māsamēkabhaktēna yaḥ kṣapēt।  
tatra tatrābhiṣēkēṇa yujyatē jñātivardhanaḥ॥  
vāmanapurāṇē---  
ghr̥taṁ ca kṣīrakumbhāśca ghr̥tadhēnuphalāni ca।  
śrāvaṇē śrīdharaprītyai dātavyāni vipaścitā॥

6f33cb3997.d: The Kokila vratam is performed for a month, beginning this day, until the Full Moon day of Shravana Masa. Performed by women, Devi Parvati is worshipped in the form of a Kokila, i.e. cuckoo, with golden wings, jewelled eyes, lotus-like face, etc. A woman performing this vratam attains happiness and saubhagyam for seven births.
6f33cb3997.s:
kōkilāvratamapyatra prōktaṁ tadvidhirucyatē।  
pūrṇimāyāṁ samārabhya vrataṁ snāyād bahirjalē॥18॥  
pūrṇataṁ śrāvaṇē māsi gaurīrūpāṁ ca kōkilām।  
svarṇapakṣāṁ ratnanētrāṁ pravālamukhapaṅkajām॥19॥  
kastūrīvarṇasaṁyuktāmutpannāṁ nandanē vanē।  
cūtacampakavr̥kṣasthāṁ kalagītaninādinīm॥20॥  
cintayēt pārvatīṁ dēvīṁ kōkilārūpadhāriṇīm।  
gandhādyaiḥ pratyahaṁ prārccēllikhitāṁ varṇakaiḥ paṭē॥21॥  
tatō vratāntē haimīṁ vā tilapiṣṭamayīṁ dvija।  
dadyādviprāya mantrēṇa bhaktyā sasvarṇadakṣiṇām॥22॥  
dēvīṁ caitrarathōtpannē kōkilē haravallabhē।  
sampūjya dattā viprāya sarvasaukhyakarī bhava॥23॥  
dvijaṁ suvāsinīstriṁśadēkāṁ vā bhōjayēttataḥ।  
vastrādidakṣiṇāṁ śaktyā dattvā natvā visarjayēt॥24॥  
ēvaṁ yā kurutē nārī kōkilāvratamuttamam।  
sā labhētsukhasaubhāgyaṁ saptajanmasu nārada॥25॥

6fcc1e49f4.d: Rakshabandhanam. One who observes this remains happy for the entire year! Note that bhadrā-karaṇaṁ must be avoided for rakṣābandhanam --- since it bestows opposite fruit!
6fcc1e49f4.s:
ētasyāmēva pūrṇāyāṁ rakṣābandhanamiṣyatē॥31॥  
sarvarōgōpaśamanaṁ sarvāśubhavināśanam।  
śr̥ṇu tvaṁ muniśārdūla itihāsaṁ purātanam॥32॥  
indrāṇyā yatkr̥taṁ pūrvamindrasya jayasiddhayē।  
dēvāsuramabhūdyuddhaṁ purā dvādaśavārṣikam॥33॥  
śakraṁ dr̥ṣṭvā tadā śrāntaṁ dēvī prāha surēśvaram।  
adya bhūtadinaṁ dēva prātaḥ sarvaṁ bhaviṣyati॥34॥  
ahaṁ rakṣāṁ vidhāsyāmi tēnājēyō bhaviṣyasi।  
ityuktvā paurṇamāsyāṁ sā paulōmī kr̥tamaṅgalā॥35॥  
babandha dakṣiṇē pāṇau rakṣāṁ mōdapradāṁ tataḥ।  
baddharakṣastataḥ śakraḥ kr̥tasvastyayanō dvijaiḥ॥36॥  
dudrāva dānavānīkaṁ kṣaṇājjigyē pratāpavān।  
vāsavō vijayī bhūtvā punarēva jagattrayē॥37॥  
ēṣa prabhāvō rakṣāyāḥ kathitastē munīśvara।   
jayadaḥ sukhadaścaivaputrārōgyadhanapradaḥ॥38॥  
sanatkumāra uvāca  
kriyatē kēna vidhinā rakṣābandhaḥ surōttama।  
kasyāṁ tithau kadā dēva ētanmē vaktumarhasi॥39॥  
yathā yathā hi bhagavan vicitrāṇi prabhāṣasē।  
tathā tathā na mē tr̥ptirbahvarthāḥ śr̥ṇvataḥ kathāḥ॥40॥  
īśvara uvāca  
samprāptē śrāvaṇē māsi paurṇamāsyāṁ dinōdayē।  
snānaṁ kurvīta matimān śrutismr̥tividhānataḥ॥41॥  
sandhyājapādi sampādya pitr̥̄ndēvānr̥ṣīṁstathā।      
tarpayitvā tataḥ kuryātsvarṇapātravinirmitām॥42॥  
hēmasūtraiśca sambaddhāṁ mauktikādivibhūṣitām।  
kauśēyatantubhiḥ kīrṇairvicitrairmalavarjitaiḥ॥43॥  
vicitragranthisaṁyuktāṁ padagucchaiśca rājitām।  
siddhārthaiścākṣataiścaiva garbhitāṁ sumanōharām॥44॥  
saṁsthāpya kalaśaṁ tatra pūrṇapātrē tu tāṁ nyasēt।  
upaviśyāsanē ramyē suhr̥dbhiḥ parivāritaḥ॥45॥  
vēśyānartanagānādikr̥takautukamaṅgalaḥ।  
tataḥ purōdhasā kāryō rakṣābandhaḥ samantrakaḥ॥46॥  
**yēna baddhō balī rājā dānavēndrō mahābalaḥ।  
tēna tvāmanubadhnāmi rakṣē mā cala mā cala॥47॥**  
brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyaiḥ śūdraiścaivānyamānavaiḥ।  
rakṣābandhaḥ prakartavyō dvijānsampūjya yatnataḥ॥48॥  
anēna vidhinā yastu rakṣābandhanamācarēt।  
sa sarvadōṣarahitaḥ sukhī saṁvatsaraṁ bhavēt॥49॥  
yaḥ śrāvaṇē vimalamāsi vidhānavijñō  
rakṣāvidhānamidamācaratē manuṣyaḥ।  
āstē sukhēna paramēṇa sa varṣamēkaṁ  
putraiśca pautrasahitaḥ sasuhr̥jjanaśca॥50॥  
bhadrāyāṁ ca na kartavyō rakṣābandhaḥ śucivrataiḥ।  
baddhā rakṣā tu bhadrāyāṁ viparītaphalapradā॥51॥

6fdad59ccd.b: Observed on Apabharaṇī nakshatra of Mēṣaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
6fdad59ccd.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

In Tiruchenkattangudi, within the Chola kingdom, there lived a devout Shaivite named Paranjyoti, belonging to a family of military leaders. He was the commander-in-chief under the Chola king and deeply devoted to Bhagavan Shiva, seeing devotion as the path to liberation.

After a successful military campaign against a Northern Indian king, Paranjyoti returned with spoils, pleasing his king. However, when the king learned of Paranjyoti's devotion to Bhagavan Shiva, he felt remorse for sending a devotee to war and rewarded Paranjyoti, urging him to focus on spiritual pursuits. Paranjyoti returned to his village and dedicated himself to worshipping Bhagavan Shiva and serving his devotees. He would not eat without first feeding a devotee of Shiva, humbly serving as a servant to them, earning the name Siruthondar (small servant).

Bhagavan Shiva, to reveal Siruthondar's devotion, tested him by appearing as a Vairavar (a Shaivite ascetic) outside his home. The ascetic refused to enter when only Siruthondar's maid and wife were home, but agreed to wait near the temple. When Siruthondar returned and learned of the ascetic, he joyfully invited him for food. The ascetic agreed, but put forth harsh conditions — he wanted to eat human flesh, specifically that of a healthy five-year-old boy, the only son of his parents, to be prepared by his parents!

Siruthondar, determined to fulfill the devotee's request, readily considered his son, who matched the description. His wife agreed, and they sacrificed their son, cooking his flesh for the ascetic. When the ascetic demanded to eat with another devotee, Siruthondar readied himself for the meal! The ascetic's request then escalated, demanding the presence of Siruthondar's son at the meal. Following the ascetic's insistence, Siruthondar called for his son, Sirala, and to everyone's astonishment, the boy miraculously appeared, alive and unharmed. They found no sign of the ascetic in the kitchen, and the cooked meat had vanished. At that moment, Bhagavan Shiva appeared, blessing Siruthondar and his family, and took them to His divine abode.
